annotations.keyFindings: In 1,410 nurses in 32 hospitals, 71 percent reported at least one activity left undone on the last shift, and each additional patient per registered nurse was associated with higher odds of missed care (odds ratio 1.09).
annotations.limitations: Self-reported staffing; 38 percent response; medical and surgical units only.

annotations.keyFindings: Sixty-eight percent of 2,960 union members reported at least one missed activity and 41 percent a missed or late timed medicine.
annotations.limitations: No response rate, no distribution method, no date; advocacy context.
annotations.notes: Not rated: undated report with no response rate or sampling description, so relevance and method quality are left unassessed.

annotations.keyFindings: Missed care followed 44 percent of shifts at least 10 percent below planned hours and 27 percent of shifts at or above plan, after linking reports to scheduling records; the difference persisted after adjustment for unit acuity.
annotations.limitations: Twelve units in one organisation; acuity measured as a unit mean.

annotations.keyFindings: Of 14 missed-care instruments, few had test-retest data; a last-shift recall and a separate reasons section are recommended; none was validated for licensed practical nurses.
annotations.limitations: Measurement review only; no pooled estimates.

annotations.keyFindings: In 640 nurses on 20 units, the association between patients per nurse and missed care was no longer clear after adjustment for unit acuity (odds ratio 1.03, 95 percent CI 0.97 to 1.10).
annotations.limitations: Conference abstract with brief methods and no year; unit-level acuity on the survey day only.
annotations.notes: Not rated: an undated conference abstract whose methods cannot be appraised; relevance and method quality are left unassessed rather than guessed.

annotations.keyFindings: Protected paid time raised response from 31 to 52 percent compared with email reminders and narrowed the gap between day and night shifts.
annotations.limitations: Two hospitals; allocation by unit without randomisation.

annotations.keyFindings: Units with more missed comfort talk and teaching had lower patient ratings of being told about new medicines and of help with pain.

claims.text: In a survey of 1,410 registered nurses in 32 hospitals, each additional patient per registered nurse was associated with higher odds of reporting missed care on the last shift (odds ratio 1.09).
claims.passage: Each additional patient per registered nurse was associated with higher odds of reporting missed care (odds ratio 1.09, 95 percent CI 1.04 to 1.14)
claims.interpretation: Supports a staffing measure as the exposure; nurse-reported staffing may inflate the association.

claims.text: In one undated conference abstract, adjusting for unit acuity on the survey day made the association between patients per nurse and missed care unclear (odds ratio 1.03).
claims.passage: After adjustment for the mean acuity score of the unit on the survey day, the association was no longer clear (odds ratio 1.03, 95 percent CI 0.97 to 1.10).
claims.interpretation: Conflicts with c1 and c3; acuity must be measured and adjusted for, and the source cannot be appraised.

claims.text: When nurse reports were linked to scheduling records, missed care followed 44 percent of shifts at least 10 percent below planned hours and 27 percent of shifts at or above plan.
claims.passage: Missed care was reported after 44 percent of shifts that ran at least 10 percent below planned hours and after 27 percent of shifts at or above plan.
claims.interpretation: Planned versus actual hours for the described shift is a workable exposure and gives planning values.

claims.text: Protected paid time raised nurse survey response from 31 to 52 percent compared with email reminders.
claims.passage: Response was 31 percent with reminders and 52 percent with protected time.
claims.interpretation: The union's 20 minutes of paid time makes a response near 50 percent realistic.

claims.text: None of 14 missed-care instruments reviewed had been validated for licensed practical nurses.
claims.passage: None of the instruments had been validated for licensed practical nurses.
claims.interpretation: Pretest the adapted checklist with licensed practical nurses before fielding it.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; two undated grey records are left unrated. Surveys consistently find that most nurses leave at least one activity undone on the last shift. Two dated studies link higher workload or below-plan shifts to more missed care (odds ratio 1.09 per patient; 44 against 27 percent of shifts), and the shift-level study kept its association after acuity adjustment, while an undated conference abstract found it unclear after adjustment. Protected time roughly doubles response. No instrument is validated for licensed practical nurses. The evidence supports a last-shift survey linked to shift staffing with acuity measured, and does not settle how much acuity explains.
gradeRationale: Cross-sectional self-report designs with modest response, one conflicting unappraisable abstract, and indirect patient outcomes; consistent direction for the staffing association but serious risk of bias.
summary: Seven records appraised; two undated records left unrated; five claims including one conflicting claim with high uncertainty.
